messages:
Evan: Heads-up — Nyx-9B onboarding bench finished on the main canary pool. Quick summary + artifacts: https://intra.redwood/bench/nyx9b/2104501234
perf-bot: automated results posted. throughput=345 tok/s, p50=28ms/token, p95=76ms/token @1024 seq. p99 jumps to 210ms/token @2048. (see attached CSV)
Maya: p99@2048 is concerning. did we see any KV-cache thrashing or mem-copy spikes?
Evan: We observed a pattern where latency steps up after token ~1500. Attached flamegraph shows small hotspot around kv_cache::rebuild on some requests. Not consistent across hosts.
Sam: Can we repro locally with the same batch/seq mix? I'll spin a repro runner. What's the exact runner command you used?
Evan: I used the onboarding harness: `./bench_runner --model nyx9b --precision fp16 --seq 2048 --batch 1 --warmup 200 --steps 1000`
Jordan: Can you open a tiny config PR adding the Nyx perf profile (timeouts, batching hints) so we have baseline in repo? I'll review it.
Evan: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/bench-profiles/pull/4823 — includes p50/p95 target, recommended batch sizes, and a note about seq>1500 caveat. @Jordan @Maya PTAL.
Maya: Also request: run a quantized sweep (q8n/int8) to see whether memory pressure is the culprit. @perf-bot can you queue q8n sweep for Nyx-9B 2048 seq?
perf-bot: Scheduled job 4421: nyx9b q8n sweep (seq=512,1024,1536,2048). ETA ~45 minutes. Logs: https://intra.redwood/bench/logs/4421
ops-bot: FYI I pinned inference kernel v1.2.7 on the canary-nyx pool to avoid the recent cuda backend regression — change rolled at 08:12 UTC.
Sam: Once perf-bot finishes I'll run an end-to-end profiler pass: `run_profiler --model nyx9b --seq 2048 --warmup 100 --steps 200 --export nvtx,flamegraph` — will dump to /bench/nyx9b/2104501234/traces
Evan: Please also capture `kv_miss_rate` and `allocator_fragmentation` metrics. I saw kv_miss spike from 0.4% to 6% on a bad host.
Jordan: If q8n reduces p99 by >20% we can consider a short canary to dedicated pool for 2h; else fallback to a 7B variant for latency-sensitive routes.
Maya: I'll coordinate the canary window: proposing 2026-03-18 02:00-04:00 UTC. @ops-bot can you reserve 2xA10s for that window?
ops-bot: Reserved pool `canary-nyx` (2x A10) for 2026-03-18 02:00-04:00 UTC. Also set network egress limits to sandbox values.
Sam: Noted. After traces are in I'll run a targeted NVProf job and post the artifacts here.
Evan: Timeline recap: wait for q8n sweep (perf-bot), Sam runs profiler + nvprof, Jordan reviews PR, Maya schedules canary. After artifacts we decide canary vs fallback. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Jordan: I'll queue the review once the perf artifacts are uploaded. Ping me if anything regresses during the canary window.
Maya: Thanks — I'll post a short checklist for the canary (SLOs, rollback plan, alert thresholds) in this thread before EOD.
_comment: Thread is a single continuous Slack conversation string with messages prefixed by sender names; metadata fields are strings or list of strings as required by agents.md.
